S & H Optometrists trades as Stephenson & Hodgkinson Optometrists, a long-standing eye care practice based in The Arcade on Main Road in Fish Hoek. The practice has been fitting spectacles and testing eyes from this address for more than 25 years, building up a loyal local following across Fish Hoek and the greater South Peninsula over that time.

The practice runs its own on-site lens laboratory, allowing prescription lenses to be glazed and edged on the premises rather than sent away, together with diagnostic equipment used for comprehensive eye examinations. A range of spectacle frames and contact lenses is stocked alongside the testing service, catering to adults and children alike. Trading from The Arcade in Fish Hoek, Cape Town, the practice remains a familiar name for residents needing routine eye tests, new glasses or lens repairs close to home.

Senior Flexonics Cape Town is a subsidiary of UK-based Senior plc, operating from Viking Place in Thornton since 1997. The company designs, manufactures and supplies thin-gauge flexible stainless steel components and assemblies, serving vehicle and engine technology applications across the automotive and related industrial sectors.

As part of a global aerospace and automotive engineering group, the Cape Town operation draws on established manufacturing processes while supplying both local and export customers from its Thornton facility. Enquiries are handled through the Thor Circle site, with free on-site parking for visitors. Based in Viking Place, Thornton, the plant forms part of Cape Town's industrial manufacturing base, trading Monday to Thursday from 8am to 4:30pm and Fridays until 3:30pm, closed over weekends.

Sentinel Primary School is a public school in Hangberg, Hout Bay, established in 1969 as one of the oldest seaside schools in the Western Cape. Over the decades it grew beyond a straightforward primary school into an intermediate school, later taking on Grade 8 and Grade 9 learners alongside its primary-phase classes.

Serving the Hangberg fishing community and surrounding Hout Bay neighbourhoods, the school has long been a fixture of local education on the Cape Peninsula's Atlantic side, with a history tied closely to the harbour village it overlooks. It is listed alongside other Hout Bay institutions in regional school directories. Located on Atlantic Skipper Road in Hangberg, the school continues to serve families in the area, offering a familiar, community-rooted option for parents seeking primary and lower-intermediate schooling close to home.

Shin Thai Asian Kitchen is a Thai and sushi restaurant trading from Eastlake Shopping Centre in Marina da Gama, serving dinner seven nights a week. The menu draws on Thai classics alongside a sushi selection, giving diners a choice between cooked Asian dishes and fresh rolls and nigiri in one sitting.

The restaurant offers takeaway for customers who prefer to eat at home, and runs a bring-your-own-wine policy, letting guests pair their own bottle with dinner rather than relying solely on a restaurant wine list. This arrangement, along with its evening-only service, has made it a regular stop for residents of the Marina da Gama canal-side suburb looking for a casual Asian meal nearby. Based in Eastlake Shopping Centre, Marina da Gama, Muizenberg, the restaurant suits diners after a relaxed, no-fuss dinner rather than a formal night out.

Shoprite Nyanga Junction is a branch of Shoprite, South Africa's largest supermarket retailer, trading from Shop 19 in Nyanga Junction Shopping Centre on Duinefontein Road in Manenberg. As a full-service supermarket, the store sells groceries, fresh produce and household goods, and also handles bill payments and other everyday financial services at the till point.

Shoprite's model is built around affordability, and this branch extends that reach into Manenberg and the greater Nyanga area, giving residents a large-format grocery option within their own shopping centre rather than having to travel further afield. Select Shoprite stores also offer grant payouts and prescription medicine collection, services typical of the chain's community-facing branches. Trading from Nyanga Junction Shopping Centre in Manenberg, the store forms a key anchor of that centre's retail offering for the surrounding neighbourhood.

Shoprite Rocklands is a branch of the Shoprite supermarket chain, trading at Rocklands Shopping Centre on the corner of Park Avenue and Caravelle Street in Rocklands, Mitchells Plain. Like other Shoprite stores, it sells groceries, fresh produce, meat, bakery items and household essentials under one roof, aimed at everyday family shopping.

As South Africa's largest food retailer, Shoprite positions its stores around affordability and accessibility, and this branch brings that offer into the heart of the Rocklands residential area rather than requiring shoppers to travel to a larger mall. The store anchors its corner of Rocklands Shopping Centre, drawing footfall from surrounding streets and bus routes through Mitchells Plain. Located on Park Avenue and Caravelle Street in Rocklands, it remains one of the more established grocery options for residents of that part of Mitchells Plain.

Simply Asia in Lakeside Centre is a branch of the South African Simply Asia franchise, serving Thai, sushi and other Asian-inspired dishes from its Main Road premises in Lakeside. The menu spans cooked options such as curries and stir-fries alongside a sushi counter, with seafood and vegetarian dishes also on offer for diners with different tastes.

Operating within a wider franchise network, the Lakeside branch follows the format used across its sister restaurants, offering both dine-in seating and a takeaway option for customers on the go, with on-site parking making it an easy stop for passing traffic along Main Road. The restaurant trades long hours into the evening, suiting both lunchtime and dinner diners. Based in Lakeside Centre, Lakeside, Cape Town, it gives the surrounding Southern Suburbs an accessible Asian dining option close to Zandvlei.

Simunye Primary Health Care Centre is a general practice based at the Three Anchor Bay Medical Centre on Main Road, on the corner of Penarth Road. Registered as a general practice (GP) healthcare provider, it offers everyday medical consultations, chronic care management and preventative health services to patients from across the Atlantic Seaboard.

The practice is staffed by family practitioners whose backgrounds include specialised experience in HIV and TB management, public health and emergency medicine, giving the centre a broader clinical reach than a typical single-doctor surgery. This community-oriented approach extends to long opening hours, with the practice open every day from early morning into the evening to accommodate working patients and walk-ins alike. Based in Three Anchor Bay, Cape Town, the centre serves as an accessible first point of medical care for that part of the Atlantic Seaboard.

Smart Laser Skin & Body Aesthetics is an aesthetic and beauty clinic trading from Brackenfell Corner shopping centre on Paradys Street in Brackenfell. The clinic is one of several branches operating under the same name across Cape Town, offering laser hair removal alongside medical-grade skin peels for face and body treatments.

Alongside its skin treatments, the clinic offers non-surgical fat-freezing procedures and facial rejuvenation treatments aimed at clients wanting non-invasive options rather than surgical procedures. Trading inside a busy neighbourhood shopping centre alongside pharmacies, salons and retail stores gives clients the convenience of combining an aesthetics appointment with other errands in the same visit. Located in Brackenfell Corner, Brackenfell, Cape Town, the clinic serves the Brackenfell and wider Northern Suburbs community looking for accessible, appointment-based skin and body treatments.

The South African Naval Museum in Simon's Town displays naval uniforms, medals, ship models and a recreated submarine control room, tracing the history of the South African Navy and its predecessors. Exhibits cover both world wars as well as more recent naval history, giving visitors a chronological view of the country's maritime defence forces.

Among its displays, the museum covers the SS Mendi tragedy, in which hundreds of South African troops died when their troopship sank during the First World War, alongside artefacts and models relating to specific vessels and campaigns. As an attraction within South Africa's only naval base town, it draws visitors already in Simon's Town for the harbour, the naval dockyard and other seafront attractions. Located on St George's Street in Simon's Town, Cape Town, the museum suits history enthusiasts and families touring the Cape Peninsula's southern coastline.

Southern Boards & Hardware is a timber and board merchant trading from Wetton Road in Wetton, supplying melamine, MDF, veneered board and shopfitting boards to the building and furniture-making trade. Alongside the boards themselves, the yard offers cutting and PVC edging services, letting customers collect panels already sized and finished for their project.

This combination of stock and in-house processing makes the yard a practical supplier for cabinet makers, shopfitters and builders who need boards cut to specification rather than raw sheet sizes only. The business keeps regular weekday and Saturday morning trading hours, closing on Sundays, in line with typical trade-counter operating patterns. Based on Wetton Road in Wetton, Cape Town, it serves tradespeople and DIY customers across the surrounding Southern Suburbs looking for board materials without ordering from a larger industrial supplier.

Southfield IT and Internet Cafe is a computer and IT services shop on Victoria Road in Southfield, offering repairs and sales covering computers, laptops and PlayStation consoles. Alongside hardware work, the shop provides general IT support for home and small-business customers who need troubleshooting, upgrades or setup assistance.

The business also runs a full office-setup service, helping customers configure new computer equipment and networks, in addition to its internet cafe facilities where walk-in customers can use a terminal, print documents or browse online. This mix of repair work, retail and internet-cafe access makes it a practical stop for residents of Southfield and neighbouring suburbs who need tech help without travelling into town. Trading from Victoria Road in Southfield, Cape Town, the shop keeps weekday hours only, closing over the weekend.

SPAR Express at Shell Firgrove is a convenience store attached to the Shell filling station on Old Main Road in Firgrove, trading around the clock. As a SPAR Express outlet, it follows the smaller-format version of the SPAR model, stocking groceries, snacks, cold drinks and everyday essentials rather than a full supermarket range.

Being attached to a 24-hour fuel station, the store is positioned for travellers passing along the route between Somerset West and the greater Stellenbosch area, as well as local residents needing a late-night or early-morning top-up shop. The combination of fuel and a round-the-clock convenience store gives motorists a single stop for petrol, snacks and basic groceries without detouring to a larger shopping centre. Located on Old Main Road in Firgrove, the store serves both passing traffic and the immediate community at any hour.

Steven Johnson Cars is a used-car dealership established in 1983, which relocated several times before settling at the corner of Milner Street and Marine Drive in Paarden Eiland in 2002. The dealership specialises in pre-owned Land Rover, BMW and MINI vehicles, giving buyers a focused stock of premium marques rather than a general mixed-brand forecourt.

That specialisation has let the dealership build up expertise in servicing, sourcing and valuing those three brands specifically, which in turn shapes the trade-in and finance options offered to customers looking to buy or sell. The showroom trades Monday to Friday from 8am to 5:30pm, with shorter Saturday morning hours and Sundays closed. Based in Paarden Eiland, Cape Town, the dealership has become a long-standing name for buyers seeking pre-owned Land Rover, BMW or MINI models in the city.

Sticky BBQ is a ribs specialist on Station Road in Observatory, built around ribs that are slow-cooked for hours, marinated overnight and finished with a sticky barbecue glaze. The menu centres on that signature dish, alongside other barbecue-style plates suited to diners after hearty, hands-on food rather than a formal sit-down meal.

Observatory's student and creative-industry crowd has made the restaurant a regular late-night destination, and its hours run well past midnight on most nights, extending into the early hours on weekends. That late-trading pattern sets it apart from most other restaurants on Station Road, giving it a following among diners looking for food after other kitchens have closed. Located on Station Road in Observatory, Cape Town, it suits anyone craving slow-cooked ribs any time from lunch through to the small hours.

Superior Packaging Industries manufactures plastic packaging at its plant on Old Mill Road in Ndabeni, handling extrusion, printing, laminating, bag-making and sheeting under one roof. This vertically integrated setup lets the company supply packaging for the fresh produce, food, dairy, fertiliser and broader FMCG sectors from a single production site.

The company holds BRC Global Standard certification at the highest AA grade, a food-safety and quality benchmark typically required by retailers and food manufacturers sourcing high-hygiene-risk packaging such as film used for fresh produce and dairy products. That certification level reflects the kind of quality systems large retail and food-sector customers expect from a packaging supplier before signing on. Based in Ndabeni, Cape Town, the plant forms part of the city's industrial packaging sector, supplying businesses that need consistent, certified plastic packaging at volume rather than small custom runs.

Sure 2 Travel is the Rondebosch branch of Sure Travel, a long-established Southern African travel agency network, trading from Riverside Mall on Main Road. As a member of the Association of Southern African Travel Agents and a business licensed by IATA, the branch operates within the industry's recognised accreditation framework for ticketing and travel bookings.

Through that network, the branch arranges flights, accommodation, car hire and travel insurance for both leisure and business travellers, drawing on Sure Travel's buying power and supplier relationships rather than working as an independent one-person agency. Being based inside Riverside Mall gives clients an easy, walk-in location for planning a trip in person rather than relying only on online bookings. Located in Riverside Mall, Rondebosch, Cape Town, the branch serves travellers across the Southern Suburbs looking for accredited, locally based travel planning.

Synergy Pharmacy is an independent pharmacy trading from Tokai Junction, on the corner of Tokai and Main Roads in Kirstenhof. As an independent rather than a chain pharmacy, it dispenses prescription medicines and stocks everyday health, wellness and personal-care products for the surrounding residential community.

Being listed with national pharmacy networks and store-locator directories gives patients using medical aid schemes an easy way to confirm the pharmacy as a dispensing point before visiting. Independent pharmacies of this kind typically combine prescription dispensing with front-shop retail, chronic medicine support and basic health advice, filling a role between a large chain pharmacy and a standalone doctor's surgery. Trading from Tokai Junction in Kirstenhof, Cape Town, the pharmacy serves residents of Kirstenhof, Tokai and the surrounding Constantia Valley area with routine medicine and health needs close to home.

Tafelberg Furnishers is an appliance and furniture retailer trading from Mamacos House on Main Road in Diep River, part of a Western Cape chain founded in the early 1960s in Bellville. The Diep River branch stocks major household appliance brands including Smeg, AEG, Defy, Samsung and Whirlpool, alongside furniture for the home.

As a long-running regional chain rather than a national big-box retailer, Tafelberg has built its business on a smaller footprint of branches across the Western Cape, giving customers a more personal, locally rooted alternative to the larger appliance retailers. The Diep River store carries stock for kitchens, laundries and living areas, from fridges and stoves through to lounge and bedroom furniture. Based in Diep River, Cape Town, the branch serves Southern Suburbs shoppers furnishing or re-equipping a home without travelling to a large out-of-town retail park.

Tafelsig Community Centre is a hall-hire venue run by the City of Cape Town, located on Olifantshoek Street in Tafelsig, Mitchells Plain. The venue has a capacity of around 130 people and includes a stage, a shared kitchen, ablution facilities and on-site parking for hirers and their guests.

Being council-run rather than privately owned keeps hire costs accessible to residents, and the venue is commonly booked for weddings, birthday parties, corporate meetings and other community functions needing a straightforward hall rather than a full events venue with catering included. Its stage makes it suitable for functions that include speeches, performances or presentations alongside the main event. Located in Tafelsig, Mitchells Plain, Cape Town, the centre gives local residents and organisations an affordable, well-equipped space for functions without booking a commercial venue elsewhere in the city.

Tai Chi Restaurant is a sushi, Chinese and Japanese restaurant trading from Forest Glade House on Tokai Road in Tokai. The menu pairs an extensive sushi selection, offered at half price on certain days, with a regular menu of Chinese and Japanese dishes for diners who want more than sushi alone.

That half-price sushi offering has become the restaurant's main drawcard, bringing in sit-down diners specifically for the deal rather than passing takeaway custom, while a separate light-meals menu caters to customers after a quicker, smaller dish. Seating is arranged for sit-down dining rather than a strictly takeaway format, giving the restaurant a more relaxed, restaurant-style atmosphere than a typical Asian takeaway counter. Based in Forest Glade House on Tokai Road, Tokai, Cape Town, it draws diners from across the southern Constantia Valley area looking for sushi and Asian cuisine close to home.

Tamboers Winkel is a coffee shop and wine bar just off Kloof Street in Gardens, built around its own-blend coffee and an all-day breakfast menu. The daytime menu suits customers dropping in for coffee and a light meal at any hour, rather than being limited to a standard breakfast service window.

From mid-afternoon, the venue shifts towards charcuterie and cheese platters served from 4pm, pairing them with an extensive by-the-glass wine list that lets customers try a range of wines without committing to a full bottle. That dual identity, as both a daytime coffee shop and an early-evening wine bar, gives it a longer trading rhythm than a typical cafe. Located on De Lorentz Street just off Kloof Street in Gardens, Cape Town, it suits anyone moving from a coffee visit into an early-evening glass of wine and a platter.

The Blue Peter Hotel is a seafront hotel and restaurant in Bloubergstrand with a history dating back to the late 19th century, making it one of the older hospitality addresses on that stretch of coast. Its position directly on the beachfront has made it a long-standing sundowner destination, with views across Table Bay towards Table Mountain.

The property runs two restaurants and two bars, giving guests a choice between more formal dining and a casual bar setting, both looking out over the Atlantic. That combination of sea views, sundowner tradition and multiple dining and drinking venues under one roof has kept the hotel a popular stop for both locals and visitors passing through Bloubergstrand. Located on Popham Street in Bloubergstrand, Cape Town, it remains best known as a sundowner spot rather than purely an accommodation address.

The Book Shoppe is an independent bookstore trading from 3Arts Village in Plumstead, specialising in restored second-hand, rare and antiquarian books alongside new titles. That focus on restoring and sourcing older books sets it apart from a typical new-release bookstore, appealing to collectors and readers looking for out-of-print or hard-to-find titles.

Beyond books, the shop stocks art pieces and serves coffee, creating a browsing environment built around cosy reading nooks rather than a strictly transactional retail layout. This setup encourages customers to spend time looking through shelves rather than making a quick in-and-out purchase, which has helped the shop build a loyal following among Cape Town's secondhand book community. Based in 3Arts Village, Plumstead, Cape Town, it suits book lovers seeking rare or restored titles in a relaxed, browsable setting rather than a mainstream chain bookstore.

The Candle Factory Shop is a factory outlet and wholesaler for candles, candle-making accessories and serviettes, trading from its premises in Clover Leaf Industrial Park in Kensington. Selling directly from the factory rather than through a separate retail store lets the business offer stock at outlet-style pricing to both individual shoppers and bulk buyers.

Alongside retail customers buying candles for home use, the shop supplies the event, hospitality and floristry trades, which rely on consistent stock of candles and related accessories for weddings, functions and table settings. That dual customer base of retail shoppers and trade buyers is typical of factory shops operating from industrial premises rather than shopping centres. Based in Kensington, Cape Town, the outlet gives both home customers and event professionals a direct source for candles and accessories without relying on general homeware retailers.

The Clarendon Bantry Bay is a boutique hotel set on the slopes of Lion's Head in Bantry Bay, offering sea-view rooms within walking distance of Clifton beach. The property is run as a smaller, individually styled hotel rather than a large chain property, with a restaurant, bar and spa available to guests on site.

Two swimming pools give guests a choice of spots to relax between the beach and the hotel itself, while the spa adds a wellness option for visitors not wanting to leave the property during their stay. Its position on the slopes above Bantry Bay means many rooms look directly out over the Atlantic, a feature the hotel markets strongly to leisure travellers. Located on Kloof Road in Bantry Bay, Cape Town, the hotel suits visitors wanting boutique-style accommodation close to the Atlantic Seaboard's beaches.

The Corner Surf Shop is a surf shop on Main Road in Muizenberg, trading since 1971 and considered Africa's oldest surf shop still in operation. That long history has let it build a reputation well beyond Muizenberg itself, drawing surfers and visitors who seek it out specifically for its heritage rather than just convenient stock.

The shop keeps a small museum of vintage surfboards on site, giving customers a look at the sport's history in South Africa alongside the current boards, wetsuits and accessories for sale. It is also known for having run South Africa's first surf-report line, an early version of the surf forecasting information surfers now get online. Located on Main Road in Muizenberg, Cape Town, the shop remains a landmark stop for surfers visiting one of the city's best-known surfing beaches.

The Daily Coffee Cafe is a branch of the Daily Coffee Cafe franchise, trading from the Balzac Building on the corner of Beach Road and 6th Avenue in Melkbosstrand. The franchise is known for pairing New York-inspired decor with local Karoo touches, giving its branches a distinct look compared to typical South African coffee shop chains.

As a franchise rather than an independent cafe, the Melkbosstrand branch follows the group's established menu and design format while serving as a neighbourhood coffee spot for both local residents and visitors to the coastal town. Its position near the beachfront makes it a convenient stop before or after time spent on Melkbosstrand's beach. Located in the Balzac Building, Melkbosstrand, Cape Town, the cafe gives the town a familiar, branded coffee option alongside its smaller independent cafes.

The Green Room is a restaurant and bar in Kommetjie known locally for its vibey, laid-back atmosphere, serving Mexican and steakhouse-style food from The Old Post House on Huskisson Way. Nachos feature among its signature dishes, served alongside steaks and other grill items, with craft beer on offer to go with the food.

The restaurant runs breakfast, lunch, dinner and brunch menus across the day, making it a venue customers can return to at different times rather than only for an evening meal, and it caters for vegetarian and vegan diners alongside its meat-focused dishes. That broad menu spread suits Kommetjie's mix of surfers, families and weekend visitors looking for a casual meal without driving into Cape Town. Located in Kommetjie, Cape Town, it has become a regular gathering spot for the small coastal village's locals and visitors alike.

The Hussar Grill is a steakhouse trading from Mouille Point as part of a South African chain that has been running for more than 55 years. The branch specialises in aged steaks, a hallmark of the Hussar Grill brand, alongside game options such as springbok and kudu and other choices including ostrich.

Beyond the steaks, the restaurant carries a wine list that has drawn awards within the industry, and the branch follows the group's chain-wide no-corkage policy, letting diners bring their own bottle without an additional charge. That combination of long-established steakhouse credentials and a guest-friendly wine policy has helped the brand, and this branch specifically, build a loyal following among steak diners in the area. Located in Mouille Point, Cape Town, the restaurant suits diners seeking a classic steakhouse meal with sea-facing surroundings along Beach Road.

The Luxe Beauté Co. is a beauty salon on Koeberg Road in Brooklyn, offering a focused range of nail, brow and hair services. Nail treatments include gel tips, polygel and overlays, giving clients several options depending on how long-lasting or natural-looking they want their nails to be.

Alongside nails, the salon offers brow waxing and tinting for clients wanting shaped, defined brows without a full lash or makeup appointment, as well as hair treatments and braiding services for clients after a change to their hairstyle. Bookings are managed through an online scheduling system, a common setup for smaller beauty salons that work mainly by appointment rather than walk-in trade. Located in Brooklyn, Cape Town, the salon serves clients across the Northern Suburbs looking for nail, brow and hair services from a single appointment-based salon.

The One 8 Hotel is a 4-star boutique hotel on Antrim Road in Three Anchor Bay, on Cape Town's Atlantic Seaboard. The property offers a heated swimming pool, a Jacuzzi and a fitness room for guests who want to stay active or relax without leaving the hotel during their stay.

Rooms are air-conditioned and include free WiFi and satellite TV, amenities aimed at both leisure travellers and business guests needing reliable connectivity during a stay. Being graded as a 4-star boutique property rather than a large chain hotel gives it a smaller, more personal scale while still offering a fuller amenity list than many guesthouses in the area. Located in Three Anchor Bay, Cape Town, the hotel sits within easy reach of Sea Point's promenade and the wider Atlantic Seaboard, with round-the-clock reception for guests arriving at any hour.

The Pool Team Tokai is a swimming pool equipment and chemical store trading from Kirstenhof Shopping Centre in Kirstenhof, part of South Africa's largest chain of independent pool stores. The branch stocks pumps, filters, chemicals and general maintenance equipment for homeowners responsible for their own pool upkeep.

Operating within a chain of independently run stores, rather than a single centrally owned retailer, gives each branch, including this one, a degree of local knowledge about pool maintenance in its own area while still drawing on the buying power and product range of the wider group. The branch previously traded from a different address before moving to its current premises in Kirstenhof Shopping Centre. Located in Kirstenhof, Cape Town, the store serves pool owners across the Tokai and Constantia Valley area needing parts, chemicals or advice without ordering online.

The Spade Boutique Hotel is a 13-suite, four-star boutique hotel and spa in Mandela Park, Khayelitsha, reported in the media as South Africa's first four-star boutique hotel located inside a township. That distinction has drawn attention to the property well beyond the immediate area, positioning it as both a hospitality business and a point of local pride.

Guest facilities include a heated outdoor pool, a gym, a spa, a restaurant and a bar, giving the hotel a fuller amenity offering than a typical guesthouse of similar size. A shuttle service is also available, helping guests move between the hotel and the wider city without needing their own transport. Located on Alfred Nzo Street in Mandela Park, Khayelitsha, the hotel gives visitors a boutique stay option inside a part of Cape Town not traditionally associated with four-star accommodation.

The Toad in the Village is a casual pub and beer garden trading from Noordhoek Farm Village, serving classic pub fare with a South African twist. Pies and wood-fired pizza feature among the more popular items on the menu, giving diners a choice between traditional pub food and a more casual pizza option.

Seating is split between indoor tables and an outdoor beer garden, suiting both cooler weather and the warmer Noordhoek afternoons when diners prefer to eat outside. Being based within Noordhoek Farm Village lets the pub draw on passing foot traffic from the village's other shops and markets rather than relying solely on destination diners. Located in Noordhoek Farm Village, Noordhoek, Cape Town, it suits casual lunches and relaxed evening drinks for both locals and visitors exploring the Noordhoek valley.

Tiger Wheel & Tyre at Sun Valley Mall is a branch of the national tyre and vehicle-servicing chain, trading from the mall on the corner of Noordhoek Main Road and Buller Louw Boulevard in Sunnydale. The branch sells and fits tyres and carries out wheel alignments as part of its core service offering.

Beyond tyres, the branch also handles general vehicle servicing, giving motorists in the area a single stop for routine maintenance rather than needing a separate workshop for mechanical work. Being based inside Sun Valley Mall means customers can combine a tyre fitment or service appointment with other errands at the mall while their vehicle is being worked on. Located in Sun Valley Mall, Sunnydale, Cape Town, the branch serves drivers across the Noordhoek and Sun Valley area needing tyres, alignments or servicing close to home.

Tiger's Milk on Long Street is a pizza, grill and burger restaurant known for dishes such as bacon-and-avocado pizza and pulled pork tacos. The menu leans towards casual, shareable food suited to groups, pairing its pizzas and burgers with grill items for diners wanting something more substantial.

The restaurant also serves local beers and cocktails, along with its own-branded Tiger's Milk Lager, giving the bar side of the venue its own identity rather than relying purely on outside beer brands. That combination of casual food and a dedicated drinks menu has made it a popular stop along Long Street's restaurant and nightlife strip. Located on Long Street in the Cape Town CBD, the restaurant suits groups and casual diners looking for pizza, burgers and drinks in the heart of the city centre.

Tommy's Chop Shop is an industrial-themed bar trading from a converted garage space in Zonnebloem, decorated with car parts in keeping with its automotive-inspired name. That workshop-style decor sets it apart from a typical bar fit-out, giving the venue a distinctive look built around its original use as a garage.

Pool tables are set up for guests who want to play a game alongside their drinks, and a resident food truck provides food on site rather than the bar running its own kitchen, a common setup for smaller bars built around converted industrial spaces. Regular live music events add another draw beyond drinks and pool, giving the venue a changing programme rather than a static bar offering. Located in Zonnebloem, Cape Town, it suits groups looking for a casual, industrial-style night out near the city centre.

TOPS at SPAR Firgrove is a liquor store attached to the SPAR supermarket on the corner of the R102 and Main Road in Firgrove, part of the national TOPS at SPAR chain. As with other TOPS outlets, the store trades alongside its host supermarket rather than as a standalone bottle store, letting customers do a grocery shop and buy wine, beer or spirits in the same visit.

The TOPS format typically carries a broad range spanning everyday beers and ready-to-drinks through to a more considered wine selection, stocked to suit both quick top-up purchases and a more deliberate wine or spirits choice. Being attached to a supermarket rather than standing alone also means the store benefits from the same site traffic and parking as the SPAR itself. Located on the R102 and Main Road in Firgrove, the store serves the local community and passing traffic along that route.

TOPS at SPAR Woodstock Quarter is a liquor store attached to the SPAR supermarket inside the Woodstock Quarter retail precinct on Sir Lowry Road, stocking a wide range of wine, beer and spirits. As part of the national TOPS at SPAR chain, the store follows the same format used at SPAR branches across the country, trading alongside the supermarket rather than as a separate bottle store.

Woodstock Quarter itself is a mixed retail and food precinct, and the TOPS store benefits from that foot traffic, giving shoppers a convenient stop for drinks while they are already in the precinct for groceries or other errands. The range typically spans everyday beers and spirits through to a broader wine selection, catering to both quick purchases and more considered buying. Located in Woodstock Quarter on Sir Lowry Road, Woodstock, Cape Town, the store serves both precinct visitors and the surrounding neighbourhood.

Traders is one of four on-site dining and bar venues at The Bay Hotel in Camps Bay, alongside the hotel's Tides breakfast restaurant, Bistro @ The Bay and Caamil's Bar. Operating as a bar venue within a larger hotel rather than a standalone restaurant, Traders draws on the hotel's beachfront position for its setting.

Guests have highlighted it among the hotel's bar venues for its beachfront views, making it a popular stop for a sundowner or evening drink while looking out over Camps Bay's beach and the Atlantic beyond. Being one of several dining and drinking options at the same property gives hotel guests and visiting diners a choice of settings within a single venue, from casual bar seating to the more formal restaurants nearby. Located within The Bay Hotel on Victoria Road in Camps Bay, Traders suits visitors after drinks with a sea view rather than a full sit-down meal.

U-turn Charity Shop in Parow is part of U-Turn Homeless Ministries' network of charity shops across Cape Town, selling secondhand clothing, household goods and furniture to the public. Proceeds from sales fund U-Turn's programmes, which are built around equipping people experiencing homelessness with the skills and support needed to move off the streets long-term.

U-Turn was founded in 1997 and has grown into one of the city's longer-running homelessness organisations, running its shops as a trading arm that generates income rather than relying solely on donations to fund its work. Shoppers at the Parow branch can expect the same rotating stock of donated clothing, furniture and household items typical of charity shops, with prices kept low to move stock regularly. Located on Voortrekker Road in Parow, Cape Town, the shop gives residents an affordable secondhand shopping option while supporting U-Turn's homelessness programmes directly.

Unimedics International is a multi-disciplinary medical and dental practice on Kromboom Road in Crawford, part of a group founded in 2015 that also runs branches in Parow and Mitchells Plain. Combining general healthcare with dental services under one practice lets patients access both types of care without being referred to a separate clinic.

Beyond day-to-day consultations and dental treatment, the group runs community outreach initiatives, extending its reach into the surrounding area beyond paying patients alone. Operating across three branches gives the group a wider footprint than a single-site practice, allowing patients some flexibility in which location they visit depending on where they live or work. Based in Crawford, Cape Town, the Kromboom Road branch serves patients from Crawford and neighbouring suburbs needing general medical or dental care from one multi-disciplinary practice.

Villa Portuguese Restaurant serves traditional Portuguese dishes such as peri-peri chicken, espetada, trinchado and seafood from its premises on Buitenkant Street in Vredehoek. The menu stays close to classic Portuguese flavours, giving diners a specific cuisine rather than a broader international menu typical of many Cape Town restaurants.

The venue doubles as a lunch spot, sports bar and dinner destination, meaning the same space serves quite different customers depending on the time of day, from a quick weekday lunch to a match-day crowd watching sport over drinks. For customers who prefer to eat at home, the restaurant also offers delivery through Mr D and Uber Eats, extending its reach beyond sit-down diners. Located on Buitenkant Street in Vredehoek, Cape Town, the restaurant suits anyone after Portuguese classics, whether dining in, watching sport, or ordering in for delivery.

Virgin Active Steenberg is a full-service health club in Westlake Business Park, offering two heated swimming pools alongside a Mind Body Studio used for yoga and Pilates classes. The club also runs a dedicated cycle studio and a separate studio for dance, boxing and HIIT classes, giving members a range of class formats beyond standard gym equipment.

A cardio and functional training zone covers more conventional gym workouts, while saunas and steam rooms give members a recovery option after training. Free underground parking is available for members, a practical feature for a gym located within a business park rather than a shopping centre with shared parking. Located in Westlake Business Park, Westlake, Cape Town, the club serves members across Westlake, Tokai and the surrounding Constantia Valley area with a wide spread of pool, class and gym facilities under one roof.

Will's Cafe & Deli is a delicatessen-style cafe on Upper Orange Street in Oranjezicht, serving freshly made sandwiches, salads and breakfasts throughout the day. The deli format gives the cafe a different feel from a standard breakfast restaurant, with prepared foods and deli-style items on offer alongside its sit-down menu.

The cafe is licensed to serve alcohol, offers WiFi for customers working or browsing over a meal, and provides parking for visitors, a useful combination for a neighbourhood cafe that draws both quick lunch customers and people staying longer. It occupies a site previously home to Carlucci's, a change that long-time Oranjezicht residents will recognise from the area's cafe history. Located on Upper Orange Street in Oranjezicht, Cape Town, the cafe serves locals and visitors to the City Bowl's upper slopes looking for a relaxed all-day meal.

WINK Cafe is a cafe inside the WINK Aparthotel on Main Road in Diep River, serving breakfasts and a la carte light meals throughout the day. Although based inside an aparthotel, the cafe is open to the public as well as hotel guests, rather than being restricted to residents only.

Vegetarian options are available alongside the main breakfast and light-meals menu, giving guests with different dietary needs a reasonable choice without a separate specialist menu. Being attached to an aparthotel gives the cafe a steady base of hotel guests in addition to passing Main Road trade, a combination that keeps it busier across the day than a standalone cafe might otherwise be. Located at Eaton Square in Diep River, Cape Town, the cafe suits both hotel guests starting their day and local residents dropping in for breakfast or a light lunch.

Wordsworth Books Dean Street is an independent bookshop trading from Dean Street Arcade in Newlands, part of the wider Wordsworth Books chain known among Cape Town readers for its curated range of fiction and non-fiction titles. The Newlands branch is particularly known for trading on Sundays, in addition to its regular weekday and Saturday hours.

That Sunday trading sets the branch apart from many other bookshops in the city, giving customers an extra day to browse or pick up a specific title when most other retailers in the area are closed. Being part of a chain gives the branch access to a wider range of stock and ordering options than a fully independent, single-site bookshop would typically carry. Located in Dean Street Arcade, Newlands, Cape Town, the shop serves book buyers across the Southern Suburbs looking for a well-stocked bookshop open right through the week, Sundays included.

Zonnebloem Boys Primary School is a public primary school on Cambridge Street in Zonnebloem, with a history dating back to 1858, making it one of the oldest schools in Cape Town. The school has operated continuously through more than a century and a half of the city's development, serving generations of families from the surrounding District Six and Zonnebloem area.

As a boys' school, it enrols learners from Grade R through to Grade 7, covering the full primary phase before learners move on to high school. Its long-standing presence in Zonnebloem has made it a familiar institution for families in the area, many of whom may have attended the school themselves or know others who did. Located on Cambridge Street in Zonnebloem, Cape Town, the school continues to serve boys from Grade R to Grade 7 in one of the city's historic inner-city neighbourhoods.
